intent: Gator connects to AI tools once per machine and keeps no vendor files in repositories
notes: Session hooks no longer write to stdout: outside a governed repository they are completely silent, and inside one the runtime advisory goes to stderr. Machine-wide hooks can then run in every repository without adding text to the model's context or breaking Gemini's JSON-only stdout.

A new machine-integration module keeps Gator's two session hooks in the user-level settings of each AI tool installed on the machine (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI). It edits only the exact hook commands Gator has shipped, compares complete entries so a timeout fix reaches every machine (Gemini reads milliseconds, so the old 5 meant 5 ms), and records each connection in `~/.gator/vendor-integration.json`.

Every ordinary `gator` command (`gator dashboard`, `gator init`, …) connects the installed AI tools automatically and silently on stdout, so `pipx install gator-command` plus one command is the whole setup. `gator hook` and `gator integration` never do; `GATOR_NO_VENDOR_INTEGRATION=1` opts out. New `gator integration status|remove|dismiss-codex-reminder`, and a "Connected AI tools" section in Dashboard Settings with the one-time Codex `/hooks` reminder. Gator never pre-trusts its Codex hook.

Repositories carry no AI-tool files any more. `gatorize` and `gator update` stop writing `.claude/`, `.codex/` and `.gemini/`, and the four Gator slash commands are retired. `gator update` removes what earlier versions left, as a planned, `--dry-run`-visible step: files that were only Gator's are deleted (deletion staged), a settings file with user entries keeps them and is left for review, and an edited command file stays. This repository's own Gator vendor files are removed here.
`gator init` now shows the runtime advisory (for example, an installed CLI newer than the repository's pin) in its banner, which is where the session learns of it now.
